correctness.rationale: For finite \(Q\), Fink's positive convolution expansion restricts exactly to \(\mathcal M_Q\), giving \(A_Q(s)=Z_Q(s)/(2-Z_Q(s))\) whenever \(Z_Q(s)<2\). If all supported integers satisfied \(a(n)\le n\), then \(A_Q(s)\le Z_Q(s-1)\) for \(s>1\). Under \(Z_Q(1)>2\), the unique root \(\alpha_Q>1\) makes the first expression diverge as \(s\downarrow\alpha_Q\), while the second tends to finite \(Z_Q(\alpha_Q-1)\), a contradiction. Fink's supermultiplicativity makes powers of one witness ample, and divergence of the prime Euler product supplies a qualifying finite support beyond any prescribed first \(k\) primes.

value.rationale: The theorem resolves a named conjecture from the primary source for every positive \(k\), rather than giving another isolated witness. It also exposes a structural bridge between classical abundance of a squarefree prime support, measured by \(\prod q/(q-1)>2\), and recursive abundance on the same support. The proof is short but non-routine: a support-restricted Dirichlet series develops a pole that is incompatible with universal depletion on that monoid.
